name: ASML’s dry 193 nm TWINSCAN AT:1150
description: The dry TWINSCAN AT:1150 combined the TWINSCAN dual-stage layout with 193 nm argon fluoride projection optics. ASML listed it at a nominal 90 nm line width. Its optics and platform were later adapted for ASML’s AT:1150i immersion prototype.

date.basis: The SEC filing date for ASML’s fiscal 2002 Form 20-F.

events.statement: ASML’s product table listed the AT:1150 as a 193 nm ArF scanner for a nominal 90 nm line width.
events.scope: Manufacturer’s product listing for the dry AT:1150.

evidence.locator: Item 4.B, printed p. 12, product portfolio table
evidence.supports: Lists the AT:1150 and its nominal feature size and wavelength and identifies AT as TWINSCAN.
Identifies the AT:1150 as the dry scanner and gives a dry-to-wet imaging comparison.

events.caveats: The filing dates the documented specification. The exact introduction, first shipment and first production use remain unresolved.

earliest_record.rationale: The March 2003 filing is the earliest unambiguous AT:1150 product listing located in this research.

research.note: Distinguishes the AT:1150 from the PAS 5500/1150 listed alongside it. The 90 nm line width is a manufacturer specification.

links.statement: The dry AT:1150 used the dual-stage TWINSCAN AT platform already shipped in the 248 nm AT:750. The platform provided the separation of wafer measurement and exposure for an ArF projection scanner.
links.scope: Shared AT platform and division of wafer operations.

evidence.locator: Exhibit p. 1, paragraph describing the launch models and the ArF roadmap
evidence.supports: Identifies the AT:750 as a dual-stage KrF model and the platform plan for ArF.

evidence.locator: Item 4.B, printed p. 12, product portfolio table
evidence.supports: Places AT:750 and AT:1150 in the same TWINSCAN product platform under distinct light sources.

evidence.locator: Exhibit 99.2, Positive Immersion Program Results, and exhibit 99.13, slide 39
evidence.supports: Describes separate measurement and exposure in the existing dual-stage platform and identifies the AT platform used for the later AT:1150 conversion.

evidence.locator: Main text, AT:750 and AT:1100 paragraphs
evidence.supports: Contemporary coverage separately identifies the 248 nm model’s dual operations and the 193 nm AT:1100 implementation of that platform. It does not identify AT:1150 component ancestry.

links.caveats: This is a platform relationship. Which AT:1100 or AT:750 components carried into the dry AT:1150 remains unresolved.
